answer.reason: The verses tell of Sennacherib's invasion of Judah, his threats against Jerusalem, and his return home and death.

clauses.english: came up against the fortified cities of Judah and took them
clauses.quote: did Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fenced cities of Judah, and took them

clauses.english: sent Rabshakeh with a great host to taunt Hezekiah and Jerusalem
clauses.quote: the king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a great host against Jerusalem

clauses.english: returned to Nineveh after the angel of the LORD struck his camp
clauses.quote: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.

clauses.english: was slain with the sword by his sons while worshipping in his god's house
clauses.quote: Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword

doubts: NAM 3:18 addresses the king of Assyria in a prophecy and may not refer to Sennacherib, so it was left out.
The 2KI 19:35 verse is not marked but is cited for the angel's strike on the camp, which context states directly.
